title: Short Stuff: Mary Had A Little Lamb
summary: Short Stuff episode on the origins and controversy of the nursery rhyme "Mary Had a Little Lamb." Sterling, Massachusetts claims the rhyme is based on Mary Sawyer's pet lamb, which followed her to the schoolhouse in 1815, and that young John Rollstone wrote the first verses. Newport, New Hampshire, instead credits Sarah Josepha Hale, who the hosts say wrote the poem. The hosts cover Hale's work as editor of Godey's Lady's Book, her collaboration with Lowell Mason on children's songs in Poems for Our Children, the melody's later British origin, the sworn statements from both women, and Henry Ford's role backing the Sawyer story and moving the schoolhouse to Sudbury. The episode ends unresolved.

entities.name: The Story of Mary and her Little Lamb

segments.title: Introduction and the Sterling vs. Newport dispute
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the nursery rhyme and the rival claims. Sterling, Massachusetts credits Mary Sawyer's pet lamb, which came to school in 1815, and John Rollstone's poem. Newport, New Hampshire credits Sarah Josepha Hale.

segments.title: Sarah Josepha Hale and Lowell Mason
segments.summary: The hosts describe Hale's career, including editing Godey's Lady's Book, and her meeting with musician Lowell Mason in Boston. Together they set poems to music for children, and the first melody was not the familiar tune, which came from a later British song.

segments.title: Competing claims and sworn statements
segments.summary: Mary Sawyer said Hale's first three verses matched Rollstone's poem about her real experience. Hale denied this and said she invented the poem. Both women signed sworn statements affirming their accounts.

segments.title: Henry Ford and the Sawyer story
segments.summary: Henry Ford backed Mary Sawyer's account, bought the original schoolhouse frame, moved it to Sudbury where he owned an inn, and wrote a book, The Story of Mary and her Little Lamb. Newport still disputes his view.

segments.title: Unresolved mystery and closing
segments.summary: The hosts note that the mystery is unresolved and read the ending of Hale's poem about kindness to animals. They close the episode.
